## 대회별 특징

### 🏆 기록 경신 추천
- **베를린 하프마라톤**: 가장 평탄한 코스로 기록 경신에 최적. 항공권도 가장 저렴
- **프라하 하프마라톤**: World Athletics Elite Label 대회로 엘리트 선수들과 함께 달릴 수 있음

### 🌍 관광 + 러닝
- **리스본 하프마라톤**: 25 de Abril 다리를 건너는 독특한 경험. 강변 코스가 아름답지만 강풍 주의
- **바스 하프마라톤**: 세계문화유산 도시를 2바퀴 도는 코스. 1982년부터 이어진 전통

## 주의사항
- **접수 상황**: 4개 대회 모두 일반 접수가 마감되었거나 대기자 명단/제한된 옵션만 남아있습니다. 공식 사이트에서 자선 단체 참가권이나 여행사 패키지를 확인하세요.
- **항공권·숙소**: 위 가격은 목업(실제 아님)이므로 실제 예약 시 가격이 다를 수 있습니다.
- **날씨**: 3~4월 유럽은 쌀쌀하고 비나 바람이 있을 수 있으니 방풍 레이어를 준비하세요.

---

### 참고: 요청 기간 밖 대회
- **바르셀로나 하프마라톤**: 2027년 2월 14일 (봄 시작 전이지만 인기 대회)

## 4월 초 날씨 (평년값)

2024~2026년 4월 관측 평균 기준:
- **평균 최고기온**: 19.9°C
- **평균 최저기온**: 9.7°C
- **월 평균 강수량**: 152.6mm
- **평균 비 오는 날**: 11.3일
- **평균 습도**: 72%

이른 아침이나 저녁에는 쌀쌀할 수 있으니 가벼운 겉옷을 준비하세요. 4월은 벚꽃 시즌으로 가모가와, 마루야마 공원, 철학의 길이 특히 아름답습니다.

## 현지 러닝 크루

교토에는 여러 러닝 클럽이 활동 중입니다:

- **가모가와 주우유카이(鴨川走友会)**: 가모가와를 중심으로 활동
- **사토우 연습회(サトウ練習会)**: 2018년 창설, 77명 회원 (여성 28명, 남성 49명). 아라시야마 합숙 등 이벤트 진행
- **교토 러너스(京都ランナーズ)**
- **KOTOKOTO RUNNING CLUB**: 교토 시내와 산을 달리는 클럽
- **화요일 밤 교토 교엔 달리기 모임(火曜日の夜に御所を走る会)**

출처: [교토마라톤 공식 사이트](https://kyoto-marathon.com/support/runningclub/), [Fat Marathon](https://fat-marathon.com/京都府マラソンクラブ・サークル一覧)

**추천**: 가와라마치역에서 가장 가까운 **가모가와 공원**이 접근성과 거리 조절이 자유로워 가장 편리합니다. 벚꽃을 보며 달리고 싶다면 **마루야마 공원**이나 **철학의 길**을 추천합니다!

Formerly the Imperial capital of Japan, Kyoto is a city of 1.5 million located in the central part of the island of Honshu, Japan. It’s one of the more popular cities to visit in Japan, 
 famous for its numerous classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, Shinto shrines and traditional wooden houses. 
The city sits in a valley and is surrounded by mountains on three sides. There are some lovely for running in Kyoto. 
NOTE: 
It is not appropriate to within temple grounds. 
A must-do run in Kyoto is the garden-like grounds of the 
Imperial Palace
, which can be combined with the nearby Nijō Castle path. The best place for a longer run in Kyoto is to choose a section of the 30 km of paths along the 
Kamo River
. 
Maruyama Park
 is another nice spot. For some hills, head to the 
Yoshidayama Hill and Green Space
 near Kyoto University. For a memorable, challenging run, head to 
Fushimi Inari & Mt. Inari
. Also memorable are the grounds around 
Myōshin-ji Temple
.
Like many Japanese cities, Kyoto is densely populated. The central part is laid out in a grid pattern. The main business district lies just to the south of the Palace, while Kyoto’s greener sections are to the north. Kyoto has fantastic transportation system consisting of municipal buses, rail, and two subway lines: the green colored 
Karasumal line and the vermilion colored Tōzai line.

Kyoto has a humid subtropical climate, which means hot, humid summers and cool winters. Runners should prepare for the heat of summer, where average high temperatures are near 33C (92F), and nights stay very warm. Winters are relatively mild, with average January highs about 9C (48F), with temps sometimes dipping below freezing, and occasional snow. Spring is delightful, highlighted by the cherry blossoms. Kyoto gets its share of rain, with greater amounts in summer due to thunderstorms.
Kyoto has an abundance of hotels, with a large number in the central business district just south of the Imperial Palace. This is a good area to stay from a running perspective, due to proximity of the Kyoto Gyoen (grounds of the Imperial Palace) and the Kamo River paths.

Walking is, of course, a classic way to explore the city. When browsing books on Kyoto, you often see headings like “Kyoto Walking Routes” or “Strolling Through Kyoto.” However, Kyoto is also a wonderful place to run. Here are three main reasons why:
Reason 1: Few Steep Hills
Kyoto sits in a basin surrounded by mountains on three sides, which means the central city is relatively flat. With the exception of some hilly areas in the east and north, there are very few steep slopes, making it easy and comfortable to run.
Reason 2: History, City Life, and Nature—All in One
From World Heritage temples and shrines to the natural setting of the Kamo River, and from business districts to residential neighborhoods, Kyoto brings many layers together in a compact area. Running through the city allows you to experience its history, culture, and living traditions all at once. Feeling the city’s terrain directly is part of the appeal.
Reason 3: Easy Navigation, Fewer Wrong Turns
Central Kyoto is laid out in a grid pattern—often described as a “checkerboard.” This dates back to the construction of the Heian period capital (794) using a Chinese-style grid-based planning system at the time. As long as you keep a rough sense of direction, it’s easy to avoid getting lost. Also, with relatively few high-rise buildings, landmarks are easy to spot: Mt. Daimonji to the east, Kyoto Tower to the south—helpful visual cues that make orientation simple, especially for visitors.
Kyoto is great for walking—but it’s just as enjoyable for running.
Finish an early-morning run and enjoy breakfast, or combine a run with sightseeing. The city is also home to many old-fashioned public bathhouses, perfect for easing tired muscles afterward. A sauna session is another great way to refresh and unwind.
Here, we’ve selected five short running courses (2–6 km) that are easy to enjoy even during short breaks in your travel schedule. Each course starts near a conveniently located station.

Kinukake-no-Michi Route: Run Through Three World Heritage Sites
Approx. 2.5 km / about 15 minutes
Gentle uphill
Our first recommendation starts at Omuro Ninna-ji Station on the Randen Line, heading north-northwest from Kyoto Station. The route passes three Buddhist temples that are World Heritage sites—Ninna-ji Temple, Ryōan-ji Temple, and ends near Kinkaku-ji Temple—along the scenic Kinukake-no-Michi road.
From Omuro Ninna-ji Station, enter Kinukake-no-Michi and follow the road. After a large S-curve heading northeast, you’ll see the entrance to Ryōan-ji Temple on your left. Soon, Ritsumeikan University appears on the right and the Kyoto Prefectural Insho Domoto Museum of Fine Arts on the left—signaling that Kinkaku-ji Temple is close.
The route is simple, but a gentle uphill continues throughout, so a relaxed pace is recommended. Sidewalks are narrow, and during peak tourist seasons there may be more people walking or waiting for buses, but please run with care and avoid getting off the sidewalks.
The name of the road Kinukake-no-Michi  (literally, the “cloth shrouded” road) comes from Mt. Kinugasa, a modest 201-meter hill located roughly between Ryōan-ji Temple and the Domoto Museum—see if you can spot it.

Approx. 2.5 km (about 15 minutes at 6 min/km)
Kyoto Station Route: From Modern Architecture to Some of Japan’s Largest Temples
Subtle bends in Karasuma Street
Approx. 2.7 km / about 17 minutes
This course begins at Kyoto Station, the city’s main gateway. From the station building, run past two of the largest Buddhist temples—Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—then loop back to Kyoto Station.
Although the area around Kyoto Station is filled with office buildings and large commercial facilities, you’ll soon encounter the impressive Goeido Gate of Higashi Hongan-ji Temple. The forecourt has been redeveloped into a spacious plaza with wider sidewalks and clean public restrooms. Continue west along Shinhanaya-cho Street to Horikawa Street, where Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—another World Heritage site—comes into view.
One point of interest on this route is the set of “bending streets.” While Kyoto’s roads are generally straight, both Karasuma Street near Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Horikawa Street near Nishi Hongan-ji Temple curve slightly eastward. This dates back to Meiji-period (1868-1912) road widening projects, when streets were rerouted to avoid temple precincts for tram lines. The shift is subtle on maps but noticeable on site.
(Route summary)
Kyoto Station → Higashi Hongan-ji Temple→ Nishi Hongan-ji Temple→ Kyoto Station

The tranquil Myojin-gawa stream running through the historic shrine district
Approx. 4.5 km / about 27 minutes
Escape the city bustle in the Kitayama area. Start from Kitayama Station (Exit 1), about 15 minutes by subway from Kyoto Station. The route passes the traditional neighborhood near Kamigamo-jinja Shrine where the Shinto shrine priests have lived, follows the Kamo River, and finishes at Kitaōji Station.
The first half winds through quiet residential streets, so watch for cars on narrower roads. After passing Ota Shrine, famous for its irises, the road opens up and reveals the atmospheric shrine-priest neighborhood (Shake-machi) of Kamigamo-jinja Shrine’s clergy.
The Shake-machi area preserves the old landscape well, including the carefully maintained riverside scenery of Myojin-gawa with small bridges, gates, and benches make this an ideal rest spot. Continue past Kamigamo-jinja Shrine and run south along the Kamo River, then onto Nakaragi-no-Michi, known for its weeping cherry trees.
Note that the adjacent Kyoto Botanical Gardens, which recently marked its 100th anniversary, is part of the Kyoto Marathon course but is not open for regular jogging.

Run the City Awake: Da Nang's Best 5 - 10 km Routes for Runners
07/06/2026
Three scenic 5–10K running routes in Da Nang, from the Han River and My Khe Beach to Son Tra Peninsula, best enjoyed before the city fully wakes up.
The best way to get to know Da Nang is to run through it before the sun gets too high
Some cities are best introduced through a taxi window. Da Nang, though, makes more sense in running shoes, especially before six in the morning, when the air is still cool, the riverside and beachfront belong to early risers, and the sea is just beginning to turn pink.
This city feels made for running. The riverfront is long and flat. The coastal road is wide, open, and breezy. The bridges sit close enough together to turn into easy loops. And when you want something that asks a little more from your legs, Son Tra Peninsula is right there, green, steep, and just difficult enough to keep you humble.
Here are three routes that are scenic without being complicated, all within a runner-friendly 5-10km range. You can take them slow and use them to see the city, or hold a steadier pace if you are training for a race. Lace up; the best one is saved for last, and it comes with a sunrise.
The riverside loop: Han River promenade and city bridges
If you want an easy first run in Da Nang, start by the Han River. This is a gentle city route in the best way: flat paths, wide pavements, morning walkers, local runners, and the river quietly reflecting the bridges beside you.
On the west bank, the stretch around Bach Dang Street toward Thuan Phuoc Bridge is an easy place to begin. You can run out and back for a neat 5K. If you want something more interesting, turn it into a loop: cross one bridge, run along the opposite bank, then return by another. Han River Bridge, Dragon Bridge, Tran Thi Ly Bridge, and Thuan Phuoc Bridge can all become part of the route, depending on how far you want to go.
Morning is the most comfortable time, before the sun gets too strong and the city is still warming up slowly. Evening has its own charm too, with bridge lights on the water, cooler air, and a livelier atmosphere. Just keep in mind that the Dragon Bridge area gets crowded on weekends, especially around the fire and water show. It is beautiful, but not ideal if you care about pace.
Anchor points: Dragon Bridge, Bach Dang Street, the Han River banks, or East Sea Park if you want to connect to the beachfront.
Distance: 5K out and back; 7–10K if you loop across the bridges.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM or after sunset.
The hill climb: Son Tra Peninsula
When you want to trade flat pavement for a little punishment, head toward Son Tra. From the base of the peninsula on Hoang Sa Street, the road starts climbing into the green. Long inclines, hairpin bends, and sudden sea views around the corners make this route beautiful, but it also deserves respect.
This is not the route for a casual midday jog. Son Tra is better for runners who already have some mileage in their legs, especially those training for hills, endurance, a half marathon, a full marathon, or a trail race. You can adjust the difficulty as you go. Running up to Linh Ung Pagoda and turning back is already a solid morning effort. If your legs are good, the weather is kind, and the road conditions allow, you can push farther toward Ban Co Peak.
The memorable part of Son Tra is not only the climb. It is the way the city disappears behind you so quickly, replaced by forest, wind, and flashes of blue sea through the trees. If you are lucky, you may even spot a red-shanked douc high in the canopy. Running here feels less like moving through a city and more like stepping into a very different side of Da Nang.
Start early, ideally around first light. Bring your own water, because there are almost no convenient places to refill along the route. Wear something visible if you begin before sunrise, and stay alert, as parts of the road are narrow and shared with motorbikes and cars.
Anchor points: Hoang Sa Street → Linh Ung Pagoda → optional extension toward Ban Co Peak.
Distance: Flexible depending on your turnaround point; hilly and better for stronger runners.
Best time: Sunrise; avoid midday.
🛵
Curious about Son Tra without running it? Try exploring the peninsula by motorbike instead, when you can slow down, stop longer, and save your legs for the views.
The sunrise route: My Khe Beach
This is the route worth setting an early alarm for. The coastal road, Vo Nguyen Giap connecting into Hoang Sa, follows the long golden stretch of My Khe Beach and gives you one of the easiest, breeziest runs in Da Nang: flat, open, wide, sea-cooled, and full of that quiet feeling of a city waking up beside you.
Start around East Sea Park and follow the beachfront path. For a 5K, pick a point about 2.5 km away and turn back. For a 10K, keep your rhythm a little longer toward Son Tra or down toward Truong Sa. This is the kind of route where the kilometers can pass almost without you noticing, because there is always something to look at: locals exercising, rows of palms, the sea, small boats in the distance, and then the sun slowly lifting out of the water.
The best window is around 5:00–6:30 AM. A little before sunrise, the sky is still blue-grey and quiet. Then the sea begins to shift into orange and pink before the day fully brightens. You may not run your fastest here, because at some point you will probably want to slow down and look. That is also the reason this route is so worth doing.
Quietly, this may be one of the most beautiful urban running routes in Vietnam. It is also one of the simplest ways to fall for Da Nang.
Anchor points: East Sea Park, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Hoang Sa Street, My Khe Beach.
Distance: 5–10K, flat and suitable for many levels.
Best time: 5:00–6:30 AM for sunrise.
Running tips in Da Nang
Avoid the heat. Da Nang is warm and humid for much of the year, so sunrise and after sunset are the most comfortable windows. Midday is better saved for coffee or a proper meal, not for forcing out a few kilometers under the sun.
Carry water. Along the beach and river, you can usually find cafés or shops after your run, but not every stretch has easy water access while you are moving. On Son Tra, you should be even more prepared.
You will not be running alone. Early mornings in Da Nang are full of people walking, jogging, stretching, and exercising by the river and beach. That friendly local rhythm makes solo running feel easier and safer.
Watch the traffic. Use promenades and walking paths whenever possible. On Son Tra, the roads are narrower and shared with motorbikes and cars, so stay to the side, wear visible clothing, and keep your attention on the road.
If you are new to running, start flat. The Han River and My Khe Beach routes are smooth, wide, and forgiving. Save Son Tra for a day when you actually want to climb.
If you are chasing a race, Da Nang hosts international marathon events during the year. Check the current race calendar if you want to plan your trip around one.

 – Tag. In Motion
      5 Best Places to Run in Da Nang: A Local Runner’s Guide
Da Nang is a pretty easy city to fall into a running routine.
Much of it is flat, the coast gives you kilometres of uninterrupted road and, early enough in the morning, even the busier parts of the city can feel surprisingly quiet. The only thing you really have to negotiate is the weather — particularly when summer decides your easy 5K should feel considerably less easy.
If you’re new to 
running in Da Nang
, though, knowing where to start isn’t always obvious. The beach gets most of the attention, but there are plenty of other routes depending on whether you want an easy morning run, a few laps on the track or something with considerably more elevation.
These are five of the 
best places to run in Da Nang
, including a few you’ll regularly find us running around with TAG.
1. My Khe Beach & the coastal road
This is probably the easiest place to start.
The road along My Khe is long, flat and simple to follow, which makes it useful for almost any distance. You can head out for an easy 5K, turn it into a steady 10K or keep going when the weekend plan calls for something longer.
Early morning is when we like it most. The temperature is more manageable, the road is quieter and the beachfront is already full of people swimming, walking and exercising before most of the city has properly started its day.
It’s also difficult to get lost. Keep the ocean on one side, run until you’ve done enough, then turn around. Not every route needs to be complicated.
For anyone wondering 
where to run in Da Nang
 on their first morning in the city, My Khe is an easy recommendation.
2. Han River & the bridges
The river is where you go when you want a bit more variety.
Rather than following one road out and back, you can use Da Nang’s bridges to create different loops through the city. Dragon Bridge is the obvious landmark, but extending north or south gives you plenty of options when you want more distance.
It’s a nice way to see central Da Nang too. You get the riverfront, city streets and bridge crossings all in the same session rather than staring at the same stretch of road for an hour.
The river is particularly good around sunrise or later in the day. Just expect more people as the evening gets busier.
Once you’ve been 
running in Da Nang
 for a while, you’ll probably end up creating your own favourite river loop. Everyone seems to have one.
3. Son Tra Peninsula
This is where things stop being flat.
Head towards Son Tra and the running changes pretty quickly. The roads climb, traffic starts disappearing and the city gradually drops away behind you.
If you’re looking for elevation, longer efforts or just something completely different from another beachfront run, this is where you’ll find it.
The trade-off is that Son Tra deserves a little more preparation. Bring enough water, check the weather and choose a distance that makes sense for your fitness. A route that looks manageable on a map feels very different once the road starts going up.
The views help. So does pretending you’re enjoying the climb when another runner passes you.
Among the different 
running routes in Da Nang
, Son Tra is probably the one we’d save until you want a proper challenge.
4. Son Tra Running Ground
Sometimes you don’t need scenery. You need a track and a session to get through.
Son Tra Running Ground is useful when you want more structure in your training. You know the distance, there are no traffic lights interrupting the session and it’s much easier to control pace when you’re doing intervals or shorter efforts.
It’s also a familiar spot for TAG runners, particularly when the week calls for something more structured.
If you’re working towards a race or simply trying to get a little quicker, having somewhere you can consistently do these sessions makes a big difference.
And yes, running laps sounds boring.
Add a group of people all suffering through the same interval and it becomes strangely enjoyable.
5. East Sea Park & Pham Van Dong beachfront
Around East Sea Park and the Pham Van Dong beachfront, you get many of the things that make coastal 
running in Da Nang
 so good without needing much planning.
The roads are flat, there’s plenty of open space and you can easily connect the area with My Khe for a longer route.
It works particularly well for relaxed runs where pace isn’t really the point. Go early, follow the coast and add distance depending on how you’re feeling that morning.
The area is also easy to reach if you’re staying around the beach side of Da Nang, so it’s a useful starting point when you’re visiting and don’t know the city particularly well yet.
When should you run in Da Nang?
Early. That’s the short answer.
Da Nang can be hot and humid, and during the warmer months the difference between an early morning run and the same session a few hours later can be significant.
For longer distances, getting out around sunrise usually makes life considerably easier. Evenings can be good for shorter sessions too, although the roads and popular areas become busier.
If you’re coming from a cooler climate, don’t be surprised if your normal pace feels harder here. Give yourself some time to adjust, drink enough water and let an easy run actually be easy.
Your watch might disagree. It’ll get over it.
Find your own Da Nang route
These five places are a good starting point, but there isn’t one definitive 
best running route in Da Nang
.
The route you keep coming back to depends on how you like to run.
Maybe that’s five quiet kilometres beside the beach before work. Maybe it’s a river loop in the evening. Maybe you enjoy hills enough to voluntarily spend your weekend running around Son Tra.
Eventually you stop thinking about where you 
can
 run and start building your own familiar routes through the city.
Running with other people speeds that process up considerably. You learn where everyone trains, which routes work for different distances and which places are better at different times of day.
And eventually you learn the really important information too.
Where to get coffee afterwards.
Run Da Nang with TAG
A few of these routes are part of our regular weeks at 
TAG Running Club
, from city runs and track sessions to longer kilometres along the coast.
If you’d rather discover them with a group, come run with us. You can find our latest weekly schedule, meeting points and session details on the ⁠
TAG Run Club page
.
Pick a session, bring your shoes and we’ll see you there.
Frequently Asked Questions
Where is the best place to run in Da Nang?
My Khe Beach is one of the easiest options for most runners because the route is flat, accessible and can be adapted to almost any distance. The Han River is another good choice if you prefer loops and more variety through the city.
Is Da Nang a good city for running?
Yes. Much of central Da Nang and the coastline is relatively flat, and there are plenty of uninterrupted sections suitable for running. The biggest consideration when 
running in Da Nang
 is usually the heat and humidity.
Where can I run hills in Da Nang?
Son Tra Peninsula is the obvious choice if you want elevation. The routes are considerably more challenging than running around the beach or river, so take water and plan your distance before heading out.
Where can I do interval training in Da Nang?
Son Tra Running Ground is a useful option for structured track sessions. Its predictable distance and traffic-free environment make it a good place for intervals, pace work and other structured running sessions.
Is there a running club in Da Nang I can join?
Yes. If you’re looking for a 
running club in Da Nang
, TAG hosts regular group runs with different types of sessions throughout the week. Check the ⁠
TAG Run Club schedule
 for the latest times, meeting points and session details.

A route along wide avenues with few turns
The start and finish are on the 
Straße des 17. Juni
, near the 
Brandenburg Gate
, which runners pass through just before the finish line. In between, the course crosses many districts of the city: Charlottenburg, Moabit, Mitte, Friedrichshain, Kreuzberg, Neukölln, Schöneberg…
The route strings together long straight sections on wide avenues, with few turns, and it is fairly sheltered from the wind. You brake and speed up less often, waste less energy and find it easier to hold a steady pace.
Worth noting: with more than 56,000 runners expected in 2026, the field is very dense, which can slow amateurs down over the first few kilometres.
An almost flat course: 116 m of elevation gain
According to the official GPX file of the course (42.28 km), the Berlin Marathon has 
116 m of elevation gain
 and 120 m of elevation loss. Elevation gain adds up every small climb along the course. The gap between the lowest and highest points is even smaller: about 25 m (from 32 m to 57 m above sea level).

The marathon is held every year on the last weekend of September, with a morning start (from 8:45 am in 2026). At this time of year, the temperature at the start is often between 10 and 13 °C (50 to 55 °F). With all these conditions combined, Berlin is the marathon where the most world records have been set: 
13 records
, 12 of them since 1998. 
Chicago
 comes second with 7.
In the men's race, all eight world records set between 2003 and 2022 were run in Berlin. 
Eliud Kipchoge
 ran 2:01:39 there in 2018, then 2:01:09 in 2022, which is still the course record.
In the women's race, Ethiopia's 
Tigst Assefa
 ran 2:11:53 in 2023, a world record at the time and the course record. She returns to Berlin this year to break the current world record: 2:09:56, set by 
Ruth Chepngetich
 in Chicago in 2024. That record still stands, even though the Kenyan runner was banned for three years for doping in 2025. If Assefa succeeds on Sunday, it will be the 14th world record set in Berlin.

## 러닝 코스

| 코스 이름 | 거리 | 고저차 | 숙소에서 거리 | 특징 | 출처 |
|---------|------|--------|-------------|------|------|
| **레이니스피아라 검은 모래 해변(Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach)** | 3km (왕복) | 0m | 약 5.4km | 아이슬란드에서 가장 유명한 검은 모래 해변. 거대한 현무암 기둥(Basalt columns)과 레이니스드란가르(Reynisdrangar) 바다 바위, 거친 파도와 장관을 이루는 풍경. 평탄한 해변 러닝. **주의: 파도가 매우 위험하므로 물가에서 안전거리 유지 필수** | [Great Runs](https://greatruns.com/iceland-unique-running-experiences/), [HikeList](https://hikelist.com/hikes/reynisfjara-black-beach-walk) |

## 현지 러닝 크루

비크는 인구 약 300명의 작은 마을이라 마을 자체의 러닝 크루는 찾지 못했어요. 대신 아이슬란드 수도 레이캬비크(Reykjavík)에 러닝 크루가 있습니다:

### 레이캬비크 러닝 크루
- **Mikkeller Running Club Reykjavík**: 매월 소셜 런 진행. 덴마크 코펜하겐에서 시작된 글로벌 러닝 크루의 레이캬비크 지부로, 런 후 맥주를 즐기는 문화  
  [Mikkeller Running Club](https://www.mikkeller.com/mrc/mikkeller-running-club), [Nord Run Clubs](https://nordrunclubs.com/clubs/mikkeller-running-club-reykjavikreykjavikiceland)

- **City Runners Club Iceland**: 매일 오전 7시 또는 오후 5시 30분에 정해진 루프 코스를 달리는 오픈 러닝 그룹. 지도가 제공되며 레이스가 아닌 일상 러닝 크루 분위기  
  [City Runners Club](https://www.cityrunnersclub.com/en-is)

- **Running in Iceland (Facebook)**: 아이슬란드 러닝 정보 전반을 다루는 영어 커뮤니티. 대회, 이벤트, 러닝 루트, 러닝 그룹 정보 공유 (팔로워 7,531명)  
  [Facebook 그룹](https://www.facebook.com/vikreykjavik/)

비크에서 레이캬비크까지는 차로 약 2시간 30분 거리라 당일 참여는 어렵지만, 레이캬비크를 경유한다면 들러볼 수 있어요.

---

**참고사항**
- 레이니스피아라 해변은 비크에서 Route 1(링로드)을 타고 서쪽으로 5.3km, Route 215로 좌회전 후 5.5km 지점에 있습니다
- 아이슬란드 남부 해안은 날씨 변화가 심하고 바람이 강하므로 방풍 재킷 필수
- 여행 시기를 알려주시면 그 달의 평년 날씨 정보도 추가로 드릴 수 있어요

			Iceland: Unique Running Experiences		
					Author photo				
Features:
										Iconic									
It’s a given that practically anywhere you run in Iceland will be beautiful, especially if the weather cooperates. But what’s especially interesting is the ability to experience some unique, one-of-a-kind runs in Iceland. Here’s our list!
Run a volcano
. There are many volcanoes that are great for hiking, but a couple are quite runnable. Our favorite is the walk up the Eldfell volcano on the island of Heimaey. About 2 km of gradual path, to the 200 meter summit. 
Full information
.
Run Where Two Tectonic Plates Meet
. Thingvellir National Park, about 25 km from Reykjavik, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Many running opportunities here on the hiking trails, which are generally flat and are a good surface. Among the highlights is the trail along the Almannagjá fault! Other good running on trails around the abandoned farms of Hrauntún, Skógarkot and Vatnskot, and the well-signed ~2 km path to the 
Öxarárfoss Waterfall. 
Run to a Natural River Hot Spring
. A wonderful hike/run is along the Reykjadalur in Hveragerdi. A couple of steeper spots, but runnable on this wide path that sits between mountain ranges, with hot springs billowing in the breeze. Your reward is a soak in natural river hot springs. Or, walk up, take a soak, and run all the way to the village. 
Full information
.
Run Around a Crater
. There are several hikes in Iceland that allow for crater viewing. One of the most impressive is Víti Maar, in the Krafla area of Lake Mývatn. A flat, ~1 km leads path around the summit, with great views into the crater.
Run In the Lava Fields
. Desolate and bleak in a uniquely beautiful way. There’s no shortage of lava fields in Iceland. Your best bet for a run is to find a lava field with a well worn path. A favorite is the Krafla Lava Fields, in the Lake Mývatn area. Combine with the Víti crater (above)!
Run on Top or Bottom of a Canyon
. Volcanoes and glaciers have helped create numerous impressive canyons. For running, we recommend the Eyjan Hill, a path along a canyon in Vatnajökull National Park, or Trail A-3 at the bottom of the same canyon. 
Full info
.
Run Along a Black Sand Beach
. There are spectacular beaches all over Iceland, but you won’t find too many swimmers or sunbathers…  For a unique beach running experience, try one of Iceland’s black sand beaches. Among the most spectacular is Reynisfjara Beach, near the southern town of Vik. 
Enormous basalt stacks, roaring waves and stunning panoramas. 
Run the Midnight Sun
. For about a month, the sun barely sets in parts of Iceland. It’s sort of a treat to run at 11 pm. The light is unique, and your running app will do a double take at the late night start. For a special treat, the 
Midnight Sun Run
 takes place in Reykjavik around the Solstice. Half Marathon, 10k, and 5k distances start at 21:00 (9pm!), and the race is followed by a midnight dip in the Laugardalslaug Geothermal Pool.
Run in Really Bad Weather
. There are lots of places that are colder and snowier than Iceland. But if you get a really bad day — wind, snow, mist, cold, blowing dust — you can have a run that the Tough Mudder folks could only dream of!  Better yet, do it near the winter Solstice, either in the dark or during the ~4 hours of daylight. A good opportunity to give your Yak-Traks and cold weather/waterproof gear a workout.
Run on a Glacier
. No, just kidding. Iceland’s glaciers are best conquered with crampons, a good guide, and a baby waddle walk.
